Covering the Secretariat beat and the Assembly proceedings was traditionally reserved for senior journalists in every newspaper. But at Dinamani , its editor, RmT Sambandam, did not believe in rigid rules. He sent a bunch of rookies, including me, to Fort St. George, known as kottai , which housed the Secretariat, to cover the Assembly proceedings.
He would send us off with one instruction: “Go and introduce yourself to the man sitting in the first seat in the journalists’ lobby.” He was referring to the The Hindu journalist, invariably the senior-most among the organisation’s journalists and, in a sense, among those covering the Assembly. The next seat was allotted to The Indian Express — now The New Indian Express — followed by Daily Thanthi , and then Dinamani .
